previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, and recent Clostridium difficile infection was readmitted with acute epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, and recurrent syncope. She reported multiple brief syncopal episodes in the morning prior to developing severe abdominal pain. Initial evaluation showed leukocytosis, acute kidney injury, and stable vital signs after IV fluids. Imaging revealed no obstruction or perforation. She was managed with IV hydration, pain control, antiemetics, and continuation of oral metronidazole for C. diff. Her pain and nausea improved, she advanced to a soft diet, and her kidney function normalized. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete her antibiotic course and follow up with her primary care provider.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ y/o F with PMHx of IDDM, GERD, HTN, depression, recurrent 
UTI's, chronic abdominal pain with extensive negative work-up 
ultimately attributed to anxiety, gastroparesis, and GERD who 
presented with one day of abdominal pain thought to be an acute 
flare of her chronic abdominal pain. 
.
# Abdominal pain: In the ED the patient was given lorazepam 8mg 
and had a femoral line placed for IV access (unable to place 
peripheral IV). During her hospitalization, her abdominal pain 
resolved with Zofran and her home tramadol. Her femoral line was 
pulled given her history of bacteremia related to venous access. 

.
# Diabetes: Her blood glucose was 374 on admission and she was 
initially kept on her home insulin regimen. She was somnolent 
but arousable during hospital day 1, thought to be related to 
the lorazepam she received in the ED and hypoglycemia. 
Somnolence had resolved by the day of discharge. She had one 
episode of symptomatic hypoglycemia while admitted secondary to 
reduced PO intake and administration of her usual insulin 
dosing, which responded appropriately to PO glucose and IM 
glucagon. She was counseled on appropriate use of insulin, 
particularly with avoiding mealtime insulin when not eating. 
.
# Leukocytosis/thrombocytosis. Her leukocytosis/thrombocytosis 
was thought to be an acute flare of her chronic hematologic 
abnormalities related to a stress response. Suspicion for 
infection was low given absence of fevers or localizing signs. 
Urine culture was positive for multi-drug resistant Klebsiella 
pneumoniae; given the absence of signs and symptoms of urinary 
tract infection, this was not treated with antibiotics. Blood 
cultures were pending at the time of discharge. 
.
==============
CHRONIC ISSUES
==============
# Anxiety. For her anxiety, she was continued on her home 
clonazepam, risperidone, and propranolol. 
# Depression. For her depression, she was continued on 
sertraline and risperidone. 
# GERD. She was given sucralfate and omeprazole for GERD. 
# Hypertension. For her hypertension, she was continued on 
Imdur, nifedipine, and propranolol. 
.
=====================

=====================

# Insulin regimen. Patient is likely noncompliant on home 
insulin regimen; consider additional diabetes management 
teaching.
